title: Historical newspaper audit for Blaschka auction and transfer discovery
purpose: Reuse the project's earlier British Newspaper Archive query matrix as a bounded historical audit for the auction module, so maker-name and generic glass-model searches are not silently rerun or misread as exhaustive coverage.

source_backend.reuse_note: The matrix was created for the microscopy/material-transfer project but deliberately included maker-specific Blaschka/Blaschke and glass-model transfer queries. Those rows are re-used here only at the level their original query log supports.

query_runs.auction_module_interpretation: Generic nineteenth-century newspaper searching for `glass models auction` is too noisy to function as an exhaustion test. Future newspaper work should use maker spelling, taxon, collector, institution, inventory number, address or named-estate anchors.
No qualifying auction event can be promoted from this maker-specific BNA row.

query_runs.original_note: Edinburgh 1867 purchase and 1871 acquisition; presented term noisy
query_runs.auction_module_interpretation: The only two retained Blaschke-model records are institutional acquisition evidence and are therefore excluded from the auction layer by policy.

institutional_exclusions_recovered_by_BN.exclusion_reason: The source explicitly describes acquisition by purchase into an institution, even though the institution name is missing from the retained preview; do not promote it into the auction layer or merge it with Edinburgh 1867 without proof.

historical_auction_search_implications: The fully screened F11 row is a useful negative boundary for that exact Blaschke spelling/query formulation: its retained hits resolve to institutional acquisitions, not public auction lots.
F09 demonstrates why generic `glass models auction` newspaper queries are unusable at scale without provenance anchors.
F10 and F12 remain partial/count-unstable and cannot support an absence claim.

The newspaper layer should now be driven by named seeds from the auction backend: Philip Brookes Mason, Science Museum inventory numbers, Berlin zoological-institute labels, Loudon's unnamed school/dealer, model numbers such as L. No. 330/343, and exact taxa.
coverage_guard: This audit reuses a bounded 1850-1886 BNA search matrix. It is not a complete British newspaper search for Blaschka auctions: some query rows were count-unstable or semantically noisy, and the matrix ends in 1886, before the Mason estate and most later secondary-market history.
